steps.step: Step 1: router and R-1 calls know global (PR 15234, merged)
Step 2: count global calls and time the US to EU path
Step 3: US calls borrow EU capacity as low-priority calls through the EU router (on top of PR 15178)
Step 4: EU lend limit set by feedback (same controller code as the low-priority limit)
Step 5: US router sends global calls to the EU router
Step 6: one Doppler key for the EU router in the US router Secret (Jean)

impact.value: 98.1% of US jobs (99.4% of pages) have no residency limit, so they can run in EU or AU. Measured on US prod jobs, Nov 12 to 18 (Jensen), reported 2026-11-18.

impact.value: 2.2% (fpp-2b) to 11.1% (citation-7b); the largest average queue is 22.0 calls (fpp-35b). In each of those minutes the EU had an idle slot.
